question: If I’m tracking a federal regulatory proposal, what’s the difference between looking in Part I and Part II of the Canada Gazette?
generated_answer:
The Canada Gazette is the official newspaper of the Government of Canada. You can use it to find out what federal regulatory proposals are on the way, including those coming from Health Canada. Part I of the Canada Gazette contains new regulations or changes to existing regulations. It also includes proposals that affect businesses or consumers. Part II of the Canada Gazette contains regulations that affect the general public, such as food safety. How do I get started? You can get started by browsing Health Canada’s List of Proposed Regulatory Initiatives. It includes all regulatory proposals currently being considered by Health Canada. You can also search for proposals by subject, keyword or other criteria.

To be eligible for the MCDP, candidates must:

Have completed a master’s degree in a discipline relevant to the federal public service from a Canadian university or the equivalent in a foreign country

Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act

Have at least three years of current and cumulative professional or volunteer experience in the last five years

If selected, candidates must:

Be willing to relocate anywhere in Canada

Meet the official language requirements of the Public Service Commission (PSC)

Be willing to work in a bilingual environment

Please note that the MCDP does not offer employment. The program provides a unique opportunity to work in a department or agency that is responsible for the development and implementation of public policy in a specific area. The program is designed to provide a challenging and rewarding experience for individuals who are interested in public policy and are looking to make a positive impact in their community.
